_comment: The catalog's own 'example' field is illustrative, not runnable: it contains
placeholders such as ' container-id' and ' --get $ipv4 --vrf $vrf-id'. This
file supplies arguments that actually execute on the node.
'args'      literal argv appended after the command name.
'args_from' a resolver that reads a real value off the node at capture time.
'skip'      documented, never executed, with the reason recorded here.
'max_lines' trim the capture to this many lines (0 = keep everything).
Defaults to defaults.max_lines. Trimmed captures end with an
explicit marker so no table is ever shown as if it were complete.
Commands in the Exec tier are refused by the script itself from catalog
metadata and need no entry here.
_scrub_profile_note: scrub_profile selects how much infrastructure identity survives.
For a company customer, infrastructure identifiers ARE personally identifiable
information: internal addressing, MAC addresses, AS numbers and hostnames all
identify the organisation. The scrub filter therefore defaults to 'strict',
which removes them, so pointing the harness at a customer node and committing
the result cannot leak by omission.
This repository declares 'lab' because its captures come from an F5-owned demo
tenant covered by the authorized-use statement in CLAUDE.md, where the
addressing IS the diagnostic content. That choice lives here rather than in the
script so it shows up in a diff and has to be reviewed.
Capturing from a customer node: do NOT set this to lab.

diagnosis._note: GLOBAL scope: captured with GET .../vpm/debug/global/diagnosis, which takes no arguments and returns JSON. Listed here so the manifest is a complete inventory of what gets captured.

health._note: GLOBAL scope: captured with GET .../vpm/debug/global/health, which takes no arguments and returns JSON.

rt._note: VRF 2 is the populated inet4 table on this topology. VRF 0 and 3 both answer 'No such file or directory'. Note that the vRouter table id is NOT the FRR vrf-id that show-ip-bgp-summary reports.
